title: Reduce APK size without regressing performance
description: Investigate what's contributing to APK size (dependencies, resources, unused code) and trim it for easier installs on lower-end devices/slower connections common among the target users, without hurting startup time or runtime performance.
acceptanceCriteria: APK analyzer run to identify largest contributors (libraries, resources, generated code)
R8/ProGuard minification and resource shrinking enabled and verified not to break any feature (needs a full manual pass, not just a successful build)
Unused dependencies or oversized assets removed or replaced
Cold start time and key screen transitions measured before/after to confirm no regression

history.note: Added from the v2 feedback session (warden interviews after the v1 field test) and from buried enhancement/limitation notes surfaced while re-reading the full v1 board history.

Current APK size is already small enough in practice - not worth the effort or the R8/minification regression risk right now. Also removes the size-vs-PDF-library tension this ticket had with LODGY-56/37/45; those are now free to pick whichever PDF approach is simplest to build correctly, not constrained by keeping the APK lean. Revisit only if a real installability complaint shows up.
